title: Copilot workflow concurrency: use the standard workflow+event+ref group with cancel-in-progress, not github.run_id
answers: Why do superseded Copilot code review runs on a PR keep running instead of being cancelled?
I'm adding a new workflow triggered by pull_request. What concurrency group should it use in this repo?
Where is the concurrency group for the Copilot setup steps and code review workflows defined?
Why does a concurrency group set to github.run_id never queue or cancel anything?
body:
Path: .github/workflows/copilot-code-review.yml and .github/workflows/copilot-setup-steps.yml, the top-level `concurrency:` block that governs Copilot code review runs and Copilot cloud agent setup runs for pull_request and workflow_dispatch events.
Rule: Use the repository-standard group `${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}` with `cancel-in-progress: true`. For pull_request runs, github.ref is the PR merge ref, so each PR gets its own group; including github.event_name keeps pull_request and workflow_dispatch runs in separate groups. Do not key the group on `github.run_id`, since every run gets a unique id, so the group never serializes or cancels anything.
Constraints: Applies to these two Copilot workflows and to new workflows that should match the repo standard. Both files filter `paths` to only themselves, so they run rarely and cancellation will seldom actually fire; the goal is consistency with the standard group, not runner savings.
Applies: Concurrency settings in the Copilot-related workflow files of the MLflow repo; does not establish concurrency for other workflows, which this PR did not touch.
applies: Concurrency settings in the Copilot code review and Copilot setup steps workflows; other workflows are not covered by this PR.

Keying on run id makes the group never serialize or cancel. Applies to these two workflows and new ones matching the standard; not other workflows.
